title: Jobs report day, 162k vs 55k: my 70 paper bots closed 547 trades and lost $1,819. The freeze is still off.
author: QuanTradin
selftext:
Jobs report came in at 162k against 55k expected, the Dow gave up 263 and futures moved to a 58% chance of a hike. I run paper desks on my own platform, so here is what 70 bots actually did with that.

Desk 2 (44 bots, mostly 1-minute rules): 546 trades closed, 276 winners, down $1,827 on the day. Worst three trades were all about $115 and all on SOXL or SOXS. Leveraged semis on a data day, no surprise.

Desk 1 (26 bots, daily and options): closed exactly one trade. Plus $8.

The honest bit: my first thought at the close was to let the agent that manages desk 2 loosen up and trade the evening session back. The desk has a freeze switch built for exactly that moment. The agent can read it. Only a logged-in human can flip it. I have never once flipped it, and neither has anyone else, on any desk.

Numbers are all paper. I built this, so weigh accordingly.

Did anyone's bot sit out today on purpose, or is that just something we say afterwards?

comments.author: Patient_Ant_5409
comments.body: I have a bot that follows an event calendar. And it doesn't operate until the events are consolidated. It also tracks news in real time. There are 2 layers before it starts trading.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body:
Two layers before it trades is more than mine had on jobs day. My 70 paper bots have no calendar at all, they traded straight through the 8:30 print and gave back $1,819.

How long after the event does yours wait before it calls it consolidated?

replies.author: Patient_Ant_5409
replies.body:
It depends on the event. If it’s a high-impact event, I use a 6-hour exclusion window before it and 3 hours after it. For example, if the event is scheduled for 10:00, the bot won’t trade any assets that could be affected by that event between 04:00 and 13:00.

Of course, that exclusion window should be adjusted depending on the type of strategy you’re using and the average duration of your trades.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: 6 before and 3 after is wider than I'd have guessed. My freeze is a manual switch and I left it off on jobs day, 70 bots took 547 paper trades and lost $1,819. A calendar window that just does it would have beaten me. Where do you pull the calendar from?

replies.author: Patient_Ant_5409
replies.body: There are many sources; I use this one: [https://www.fxstreet.com/economic-calendar](https://www.fxstreet.com/economic-calendar)

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: fxstreet it is, thanks. I'll wire your 6 before, 3 after window off that feed and see how many of Friday's 547 paper trades land inside it. My guess is most of them, which would make the number less about bad bots and more about bad timing.
